grammar.meaning: ≈ names a person, place, thing or idea. e.g. echo, matrix, truth
≈ stands in for a noun. e.g. he, it, they, itself
≈ an action or state. e.g. govern, flow, is
≈ describes a noun. e.g. general, latent, whole
≈ describes a verb, adjective or adverb. e.g. inwardly, very, now
≈ relates a noun to the rest of the sentence. e.g. in, of, through, under
≈ joins words or clauses. e.g. and, but, or, because
≈ specifies a noun. e.g. the, a, this, every
≈ an exclamation. e.g. oh, yes
≈ who or what the sentence is about. e.g. [ECHO] reads itself
≈ what is said about the subject. e.g. ECHO [reads itself]
≈ receives the action. e.g. ECHO reads [the matrix]
≈ to or for whom the action is done. e.g. give [him] the word
≈ completes the meaning of a verb. e.g. truth is [a seal]
≈ adds detail to another word or phrase. e.g. the [silent] breath
≈ a noun and its modifiers. e.g. the first letter
≈ a verb and its objects and modifiers. e.g. opens the matrix
≈ a preposition and its object. e.g. into the canvas
≈ an adjective and its modifiers. e.g. very general
≈ an adverb and its modifiers. e.g. quite slowly
≈ a complete thought with subject and verb. e.g. Echo reads itself
≈ a clause that cannot stand alone. e.g. because Resh governs
≈ modifies a noun, often with who, which, that. e.g. the letter that seals
≈ one independent clause. e.g. The matrix opens.
≈ two independent clauses joined. e.g. Ayin perceives, and Pe expresses.
≈ an independent clause with a dependent clause. e.g. When ר reads itself, the matrices open.
≈ states something. e.g. The head governs.
≈ asks something. e.g. What governs?
≈ commands something. e.g. Open the matrix.
≈ expresses strong feeling. e.g. It opened!
≈ when the action happens: past, present, future. e.g. read, reads, will read
≈ how the action unfolds: simple, progressive, perfect. e.g. reads, is reading, has read
≈ the speaker's stance: indicative, imperative, subjunctive. e.g. if it were open
≈ whether the subject acts (active) or is acted on (passive). e.g. Echo opens it / it is opened
≈ speaker, addressee, other: 1st, 2nd, 3rd. e.g. I, you, he
≈ singular or plural. e.g. word, words
≈ subject and verb match in person and number. e.g. he reads / they read
≈ English places Subject, Verb, Object in that order. e.g. Echo (S) reads (V) letters (O)
≈ whether a verb takes an object. e.g. seal the letter / the letter rests
≈ the smallest unit of meaning: root, prefix, suffix. e.g. trans + form + ation

symbols.meaning: ≈ plus: addition; also positive charge. e.g. a + b
≈ minus: subtraction; negation. e.g. a − b
≈ times: multiplication; · also dot product. e.g. F = m · a
≈ divided by: division; ratio. e.g. v = d / t
≈ equals: both sides are the same value. e.g. E = mc²
≈ not equal: the sides differ. e.g. a ≠ b
≈ approximately equal: close in value; in the DSL, a field of meaning. e.g. π ≈ 3.14
≈ identical / defined as: true by definition; congruence. e.g. a ≡ b (mod n)
≈ proportional to: grows in fixed ratio. e.g. F ∝ 1/r²
≈ less than, greater than: order. e.g. x < y
≈ at most, at least: order including equality. e.g. 0 ≤ p ≤ 1
≈ plus or minus: both signs; uncertainty. e.g. x = 2 ± 0.1
≈ square root: the number that squared gives this. e.g. √4 = 2
≈ power: multiply x by itself n times. e.g. r²
≈ absolute value / magnitude: size without sign or direction. e.g. |v|
≈ norm: length of a vector. e.g. ‖x‖
≈ sum: add a series of terms. e.g. ∑ᵢ xᵢ
≈ product: multiply a series of terms. e.g. ∏ᵢ xᵢ
≈ integral: accumulate over a range; area under a curve. e.g. ∫ f(x) dx
≈ contour integral: integral around a closed path. e.g. ∮ E · dA
≈ derivative: rate of change. e.g. dv/dt = a
≈ partial derivative: rate of change in one variable. e.g. ∂u/∂t
≈ nabla / gradient: direction and rate of steepest change. e.g. ∇φ
≈ divergence, curl: outflow and rotation of a field. e.g. ∇·E = ρ/ε₀
≈ delta / change: difference between two states. e.g. Δx
≈ small change; variation: an infinitesimal or small difference. e.g. (S+δ)−S = δ
≈ limit: value approached. e.g. lim x→0
≈ infinity: without bound. e.g. n → ∞
≈ tends to; maps to; yields: approach, function mapping, or reaction direction. e.g. x → 0; A → B
≈ equilibrium: reaction runs both ways. e.g. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃
≈ element of, not element of: membership in a set. e.g. x ∈ ℝ
≈ subset: contained within a set. e.g. A ⊂ B
≈ union, intersection: combine sets, or keep what they share. e.g. A ∪ B
≈ empty set: the set with nothing in it. e.g. A ∩ B = ∅
≈ number sets: natural, integer, rational, real, complex. e.g. x ∈ ℂ
≈ for all, there exists: quantifiers of logic. e.g. ∀x ∃y
≈ not, and, or: logical operators. e.g. p ∧ ¬q
≈ implies, if and only if: logical consequence and equivalence. e.g. p ⇒ q
≈ therefore, because: steps in a proof. e.g. ∴ x = 2
≈ tensor product, direct sum (or XOR): combining spaces or values. e.g. V ⊗ W
≈ composition: apply one function after another. e.g. f ∘ g
≈ angle brackets: inner product; quantum state. e.g. ⟨ψ|φ⟩
≈ pi: circle ratio ≈ 3.14159. e.g. C = 2πr
≈ Euler's number: ≈ 2.71828, base of natural growth. e.g. eˣ
≈ imaginary unit: i² = −1. e.g. e^(iπ) + 1 = 0
≈ golden ratio; also angle or field: ≈ 1.618 as the golden ratio. e.g. φ = (1+√5)/2
≈ angle, angular frequency: rotation and its rate. e.g. ω = 2πf
≈ wavelength; eigenvalue; decay constant: depends on domain. e.g. c = fλ
≈ mean, standard deviation: center and spread of data. e.g. μ ± σ
≈ density; charge density; correlation: depends on domain. e.g. ρ = m/V
≈ permittivity and permeability of free space: electromagnetic constants. e.g. c = 1/√(ε₀μ₀)
≈ speed of light: 299,792,458 m/s. e.g. E = mc²
≈ gravitational constant: 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². e.g. F = Gm₁m₂/r²
≈ Planck constant, reduced Planck constant: quantum of action; ħ = h/2π. e.g. E = hf
≈ Boltzmann constant: links temperature and energy. e.g. E = k_B T
≈ Avogadro constant: 6.022 × 10²³ per mole. e.g. n = N/N_A
≈ gas constant: 8.314 J/(mol·K). e.g. PV = nRT
≈ degree: angle or temperature. e.g. 90°, 25 °C
≈ perpendicular, parallel: geometric relations. e.g. a ⊥ b
≈ angle, triangle: geometric objects. e.g. ∠ABC
≈ congruent, similar: same shape and size, or same shape. e.g. △ABC ≅ △DEF
≈ wavefunction: quantum state of a system. e.g. Ĥψ = Eψ
≈ Hamiltonian operator: total energy operator. e.g. Ĥψ = Eψ

formulas.name: Newton's Second Law
formulas.law: Force equals mass times acceleration — the fundamental relation between cause (force) and effect (acceleration) in the Natural Domain

formulas.name: Kinetic Energy
formulas.law: Energy of motion — a state of the entity determined by its mass and velocity

formulas.name: Potential Energy (gravitational)
formulas.law: Energy stored in position within a gravitational field

formulas.name: Work-Energy Theorem
formulas.law: Work done equals force times displacement in the direction of force

formulas.name: Conservation of Energy
formulas.law: Total energy is conserved — a state that cannot be destroyed, only transformed

formulas.name: Momentum
formulas.law: Quantity of motion — a state of entity determined by mass and velocity

formulas.name: Conservation of Momentum
formulas.law: Total momentum is conserved in an isolated system

formulas.name: Uniform Motion
formulas.law: Distance equals velocity times time — the discretization of continuous motion into finite steps

formulas.name: Equation of Motion
formulas.law: Velocity changes linearly with time under constant acceleration

formulas.name: Gravitational Force
formulas.law: Gravitational attraction between masses — inverse square law

formulas.name: Orbital Velocity
formulas.law: Speed required for circular orbit — balance of gravitational and centripetal force

formulas.name: Ideal Gas Law
formulas.law: State equation of an ideal gas — pressure, volume, and temperature are mutually constraining

formulas.name: First Law of Thermodynamics
formulas.law: Energy is conserved: internal energy change equals heat added minus work done

formulas.name: Entropy Change
formulas.law: Entropy measures disorder — heat at temperature T changes entropy by Q/T

formulas.name: Boltzmann Entropy
formulas.law: Statistical definition of entropy — connects macroscopic state to microscopic counting

formulas.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Law
formulas.law: Radiated power proportional to fourth power of temperature

formulas.name: Coulomb's Law
formulas.law: Electric force between charges — same structure as gravitational law

formulas.name: Electric Field
formulas.law: Electric field is force per unit charge at a point in space

formulas.name: Ohm's Law
formulas.law: Voltage equals current times resistance — linear relation between cause (voltage) and effect (current)

formulas.name: Electric Power
formulas.law: Power dissipated in a circuit — three equivalent forms

formulas.name: Capacitance
formulas.law: Capacity to store charge per unit voltage

formulas.name: Magnetic Force
formulas.law: Force on a moving charge in a magnetic field — cross product relation

formulas.name: Faraday's Law
formulas.law: Changing magnetic flux induces EMF — the basis of electromagnetic induction

formulas.name: Maxwell's Equation (Gauss)
formulas.law: Total electric flux through closed surface equals enclosed charge

formulas.name: Planck-Einstein Relation
formulas.law: Energy of a photon — the bridge between wave (frequency) and particle (energy) descriptions

formulas.name: de Broglie Wavelength
formulas.law: Every particle has an associated wavelength — wave-particle duality Law

formulas.name: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
formulas.law: Position and momentum cannot be simultaneously known with arbitrary precision

formulas.name: Schrödinger Equation (time-dependent)
formulas.law: Evolution of quantum state in time — the Laws of quantum dynamics

formulas.name: Energy Levels (hydrogen)
formulas.law: Discrete energy states of hydrogen atom — first quantized energy spectrum

formulas.name: Photoelectric Effect
formulas.law: Photon ejects electron if its energy exceeds the work function

formulas.name: Mass-Energy Equivalence
formulas.law: Mass and energy are equivalent — the most famous Law in physics

formulas.name: Time Dilation
formulas.law: Moving clocks run slower — time is relative to the observer

formulas.name: Length Contraction
formulas.law: Moving objects appear shorter in the direction of motion

formulas.name: Relativistic Energy
formulas.law: General energy-momentum relation — E=mc² is the special case p=0

formulas.name: Lorentz Factor
formulas.law: Scale factor for relativistic effects — diverges as v→c

formulas.name: Pythagorean Theorem
formulas.law: Fundamental relation in Euclidean geometry — discovered, not invented

formulas.name: Euler's Formula
formulas.law: The most beautiful formula — connects e, π, i, cos, sin in one expression

formulas.name: Euler's Identity
formulas.law: Five fundamental constants unified — often called the most beautiful equation

formulas.name: Taylor Series
formulas.law: Any smooth function expressible as infinite polynomial — bridge between discrete and continuous

formulas.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
formulas.law: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations — the deepest theorem of calculus

formulas.name: Bayes' Theorem
formulas.law: How prior probability updates given new evidence — the Law of rational belief revision

formulas.name: Normal Distribution
formulas.law: The bell curve — emerges from the Central Limit Theorem as the universal distribution

formulas.name: Fourier Transform
formulas.law: Decomposes any signal into constituent frequencies — bridge between time and frequency domains

formulas.name: Euler-Lagrange Equation
formulas.law: Equations of motion from energy — the variational principle formulation of dynamics

formulas.name: Navier-Stokes Equation
formulas.law: Motion of viscous fluid — one of the Millennium Prize unsolved problems

formulas.name: Avogadro's Number
formulas.law: Number of particles in one mole — bridges microscopic and macroscopic scales

formulas.name: Arrhenius Equation
formulas.law: Temperature dependence of reaction rate — activation energy barrier

formulas.name: Henderson-Hasselbalch
formulas.law: pH of buffer solution — used in biochemistry to maintain biological pH

formulas.name: Beer-Lambert Law
formulas.law: Absorbance proportional to concentration — basis of spectrophotometry
